audit_findings.title: Retained OxyChem liabilities may be absent from both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.663 billion recorded discontinued-operation environmental remediation liability at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.49 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained-liability payments are excluded from continuing-operation OE, while the bridge adds cash and stakes without deducting the corresponding obligation.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, under the Purchase Agreement, there are post-closing indemnification obligations for (i) legacy environmental liabilities and (ii) pre-closing liabilities of OxyChem, including pre-closing environmental liabilities, in each case, subject to certain limitations and procedures.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch for the recorded environmental liability. The amount equals about 5.0% of base equity value, before unquantified indemnification exposure or reasonably possible additional environmental losses, and is large enough to affect the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $1.663 billion reserve and every other retained OxyChem indemnity to June 2026 liabilities, then rerun either with a probability- and timing-adjusted bridge deduction or with the associated cash payments included in projected OE, without using both treatments.

audit_findings.title: The $2.3 billion Tronox tax claim may be an omitted common-equity obligation
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.4 billion at June 30, 2026, equal to $2.15 per diluted share and 7.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The recognized tax-and-interest liability requires a bridge deduction or probability-weighted projected cash payment; historical accounting charges do not fund the future settlement.
audit_findings.evidence: However, in that event, as of December 31, 2025, the Company would be required to repay approximately $ 1.4 billion in federal and state taxes and accrued interest of $ 0.9 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates that the liability exists and is included in other liabilities, while the supplied bridge does not deduct it. Although payment depends on the litigation outcome, the filed exposure is material relative to the $33.342 billion base equity value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the exact June 2026 carrying liability and litigation status, assign documented outcome probabilities and payment timing, and rerun with the expected present value deducted from the bridge or included once in projected OE.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method stakes may be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $705 million of 2025 dividends, equal to 37.4% of anchor OE, potentially overlapping the $2.695 billion stakes bridge; actual overlap unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If investee earnings or distributions remain in OE while the related investments are also added in stakes_net, both the income stream and underlying asset value are credited to equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Dividends received from equity investments were $ 705 million, $ 682 million and $ 571 million to the Company in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Double counting is not demonstrated because the OE purge schedule was not supplied, but the filed dividends are large relative to $1.886 billion of anchor OE. Even partial recurring overlap could materially change operating value, and the stated interest-income purge does not resolve equity-method income or distributions.
audit_findings.action: Produce an asset-by-asset stakes_net schedule and an annual OE reconciliation for WES, DEL and every other included stake, removing all associated earnings, distributions, gains, losses and expenses before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter may leave sold-asset earnings in the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Pre-sale OE from divested properties may remain in the 2025 anchor even though the latest bridge already reflects the $2.3 billion of proceeds through cash, debt repayment or other balance-sheet uses.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, the Company sold non-core assets for $ 2.3 billion which included working interests in the Permian Basin for proceeds of approximately $ 800 million, non-operated proved and unproved royalty and mineral interests in the DJ Basin for proceeds of approximately $ 840 million and certain gas gathering assets in the Permian Basin for approximately $ 580 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The sale and null perimeter are demonstrated, but the filings do not provide the disposed assets' net OE contribution. The assets represented $2.3 billion of proceeds and 57 MMboe, or about 1.2% of year-end proved reserves, but those figures cannot establish the effect on sustainable OE after maintenance capital and working capital.
audit_findings.action: Obtain property-level 2025 revenue, operating costs, taxes, maintenance capital and working-capital effects through each closing date; remove their net OE from the anchor and verify how every dollar of proceeds appears in June 2026 cash or debt.

audit_findings.title: STRATOS NCI has a preferential economic claim not captured by a share count
audit_findings.mechanism: The distribution and liquidation waterfall, contingent payments and possible call obligation alter the portion of consolidated STRATOS cash flows attributable to common equity; ordinary diluted shares cannot capture those claims.
audit_findings.evidence: Dividends from the joint venture will be distributed preferentially to the NCI up to a return threshold, then preferentially to the Company thereafter.
audit_findings.explanation: The preferential rights are demonstrated and the June filing reports $635 million of NCI against $1.3 billion of joint-venture construction in progress, but the return threshold, contingent-payment exposure and call price are absent. The record therefore cannot determine the incremental reduction in common-equity value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the joint-venture waterfall, return threshold, remaining contingent payments, liquidation preference and call formula; model partner and Occidental cash flows separately and rerun OE using only the cash flows attributable to common equity.

audit_findings.title: Conditional abandonment obligations may escape both current OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.656 billion recorded ARO at June 30, 2026, equal to $3.28 per diluted share and 11.0% of base equity value; conditional AROs unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If settlement cash is not deducted in OE and no bridge liability is recognized, abandonment costs are omitted; conditional plant-decommissioning obligations can also make terminal maintenance requirements incomplete.
audit_findings.evidence: At a certain number of its facilities, the Company has identified conditional AROs that are related mainly to plant decommissioning.
audit_findings.explanation: The escape is not yet demonstrated because historical OE treatment of ARO settlements was not supplied. Nevertheless, the recorded ARO alone is material relative to the valuation, and the filing confirms additional conditional obligations whose fair value cannot yet be estimated.
audit_findings.action: Trace annual ARO accretion, revisions, capitalized additions and cash settlements through every OE year; reconcile the June 2026 recorded ARO to projected payments, add a documented allowance for conditional facilities when estimable, and rerun using either OE cash deductions or a present-value bridge deduction without double counting.
